nodes.description: Immutable ERC20 token address that is distributed by the Merkle distributor.
Immutable Merkle root used to validate distribution claims.
Packed bitmap tracking which claim indexes have already been claimed.
Address of the contract owner used for access control.
External function that verifies a Merkle proof, marks the index claimed and transfers tokens to the account.
Only-owner function that transfers the whole token balance of the contract to a recipient.
View function returning whether a given index has already been claimed.
Private function that sets the bit for a given index in claimedBitMap.
View function returning the token balance currently held by the contract.
Constructor that sets the immutable token address and Merkle root.
Caller address used by the onlyOwner modifier for access control.
External ERC20 transfer call that sends tokens to the claiming account inside claim().
External ERC20 transfer call that sends the whole contract balance to the recipient inside withdraw().
Claim index identifying the leaf in the Merkle tree and the claimed bitmap position.
Recipient account for the claimed tokens.
Amount of tokens to transfer in the claim.
Merkle proof used to verify the leaf against merkleRoot.
Recipient address of the tokens withdrawn by the owner.
Hashed leaf node keccak256(abi.encodePacked(index, account, amount)) verified against the Merkle root.

edges.reason: The claim index parameter is passed into isClaimed to check whether it has already been claimed.
The claim index parameter is passed into _setClaimed to mark it as claimed.
isClaimed reads the claimedBitMap state variable to determine claim status.
_setClaimed writes the claimedBitMap state variable to record the claim.
The account parameter is encoded into the Merkle leaf node hash.
The index parameter is encoded into the Merkle leaf node hash.
The amount parameter is encoded into the Merkle leaf node hash.
The merkleProof parameter is consumed by MerkleProof.verify inside claim().
The merkleRoot state variable is used as the trusted root when verifying the proof in claim().
The account parameter is used as the recipient of the external token transfer.
The amount parameter is used as the value of the external token transfer.
The token state variable is the ERC20 contract on which transfer is invoked in claim().
The recipient parameter is used as the destination of the external token transfer.
The token state variable is the ERC20 contract on which transfer is invoked in withdraw().
claim() executes the external token transfer after marking the index as claimed.
withdraw() executes the external token transfer to the recipient.
msg.sender is checked by the onlyOwner modifier before withdraw() can execute.
The _owner state variable is compared with the caller to gate withdraw().
Only the owner can reach the external token transfer inside withdraw().
The external ERC20 transfer hands control to an arbitrary token contract while claim() state is not fully finalized, enabling reentrancy.
The external ERC20 transfer in withdraw() transfers control to a potentially malicious token contract before completion.

normalization_plan.reason: The index parameter exists only to key the claim in the Merkle tree and bitmap, so it is folded into the claim function.
The account parameter is only used inside claim for hashing and as the transfer recipient, so it merges into claim.
The amount parameter is only used inside claim for hashing and as the transfer value, so it merges into claim.
The merkleProof parameter is only consumed by MerkleProof.verify within claim, so it merges into claim.
The recipient parameter is only used as the destination of the token transfer inside withdraw, so it merges into withdraw.
The node local variable is only the intermediate hash verified inside claim, so it merges into claim.
